skill: Solve an inhibited decay IVP by separation of variables, determine the integration constant from an initial temperature, then evaluate and round a future temperature; in moderate cases infer the rate constant from a second observation and solve logarithmically for a target time.
reasoning_steps: Recognize dT/dt=-k(T-S) with k>0 and T>S.
Separate, integrate ln|T-S|=-kt+C, exponentiate to T=S+K exp(-kt).
Easy: substitute given k and future time, then round temperature to nearest integer.
Moderate: infer k=-ln((Tobs-S)/(T0-S))/tobs and solve t=-ln((Ttarget-S)/(T0-S))/k; round to nearest minute.
response_contract: All eleven stored source questions use one radio field named selection and five math choices with temperature units for easy, minutes for moderate. The canonical example has a worked solution but no captured answer field.
difficulty: Requested easy matches the direct specified-rate evaluation family. Five moderate stored questions require additional calibration and inversion; no captured hard question.
invariants: Positive decay coefficient, initial temperature above equilibrium, positive times; cooling approaches equilibrium from above.
Temperature scales remain consistent within an instance.
Single rounded integer result, one correct option among five distinct choices.
Solutions retain separation, integration, initial-condition substitution and final evaluation; moderate adds observation calibration and target inversion.
permitted_variations: Ambient and initial temperatures, positive rate and elapsed time can vary independently subject to cooling and reasonable workload.
Cooling object and Celsius/Fahrenheit are incidental context; units must propagate consistently.
Rounded answer, option position, numeric rank and distractor distribution are eligible answer-bearing assignments; no source-based justification fixes any of them.
Moderate observation and target temperatures and times can vary while preserving the same calibration/inversion stages; target need not always be later than the observation if wording remains clear.
Easy must continue asking a future temperature, rather than importing moderate unknown-rate or time-inversion work.
